info.title: 12id Platform API
info.description: Issue and verify AnonCreds credentials with holders running the 12id SDK. Commands are asynchronous: they return the exchange record immediately and progress arrives through signed webhooks (or polling). Ids are stable per tenant.

post.description: Asynchronous. Returns the exchange immediately in state `offer-sent`; `credential-issued` means the holder received it, `done` that it acknowledged. Attribute values are strings; `expiresOn` is the expiry date as `YYYYMMDD` (UTC), today or later: the credential is accepted through the end of that day. At most 125 attributes, names up to 100 characters, values up to 4 KB, and 64 KB in all. `credentialDefinitionId` accepts the catalogue id or the ledger id.

post.summary: Erase the personal data of a credential exchange
post.description: Removes the personal data of this credential exchange (its attribute values) everywhere the platform holds it (the exchange record in the agent, webhook delivery bodies, biometric scores) and keeps the record itself with its ids, state and timestamps, so lists and history stay whole. Only finished exchanges (`done`, `abandoned`, `declined`) can be erased; a running one answers 409. Repeating the call is harmless. A `record.erased` webhook follows. The credential in the holder's wallet is not affected.

reason.description: Why the data is erased; recorded in the audit log. Required from operators.

Only finished exchanges (`done`, `abandoned`, `declined`) can be erased; a running one answers 409. Repeating the call is harmless. A `record.erased` webhook follows. The credential in the holder's wallet is not affected.

post.summary: Erase a connection and every exchange on it
post.description: Removes the personal data of this connection (the holder's label) and of every credential and proof exchange on it everywhere the platform holds it (the exchange record in the agent, webhook delivery bodies, biometric scores) and keeps the record itself with its ids, state and timestamps, so lists and history stay whole. Only finished exchanges (`done`, `abandoned`, `declined`) can be erased; a running one answers 409. Repeating the call is harmless. A `record.erased` webhook follows. The credential in the holder's wallet is not affected. The agent drops the connection, so the holder can no longer reach this tenant through it. `erasedExchanges` lists the exchanges erased along with it.

get.description: Every step of the biometric gate for this exchange, oldest first: attempts with liveness and match scores against the thresholds, decisions, and what the platform did with the exchange. Never contains images. `biometric` is null when the exchange was not gated.

post.description:
One wallet per SDK installation. The returned `walletToken` is shown once; pass it to your app, which gives it to the SDK. The platform never learns who the end user is; `externalId` is your own reference (for example your user id, shared by that user's devices) and is echoed in `wallet.sync_requested` webhooks.

Retries: send your app's installation id (a UUID the app generates once and keeps) as `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and body returns the **same wallet with a new `walletToken`**, and earlier tokens for that wallet stop working, so always give the app the most recent token. Tokens are never stored. While the first request is still running, a retry answers 409 `idempotency_in_progress`; retry after `Retry-After` seconds. If that wallet was revoked, a retry answers 409 `wallet_revoked`.

delete.description: Revokes the wallet token at once: the app gets 401 and the platform stops mapping mediator webhooks to it. The device keeps its local data. 30 days later the platform also removes its mediator connection, so the app can no longer receive messages; it must call reset() and credentials are issued again. Wallets that never connected to the mediator are revoked by the platform after 7 days (revokedReason never_connected).

post.description: Uses one attempt. `captureModules` lists the capture add-ons the app includes; `clientConfig` is for that add-on only.
The platform fetches the result from the vendor itself; `clientOutput` is only what the add-on returned. 409 `result_not_ready` means the vendor is still processing: retry after a second.
